title: Trump Weighs His Options in Carrying Out New Strikes in Iran
description_short: Trump Weighs His Options in Carrying Out New Strikes in Iran
description_medium: By May 22, 2026, Trump was considering possible additional strikes on Iran. A New York Times report listed energy facilities, the underground nuclear site at Isfahan, and missile sites as potential targets. Reuters had earlier reported that Trump said the United States might need to strike again. Both reports describe options under discussion, not a new strike order.
subcategory: Reported consideration of possible further strikes on Iran
notes: Reason: The Times and Reuters pages returned HTTP 403 and 401 during focused retrieval. Their supplied headlines identify possible targets and consideration of another strike, but no decision, timeline or outcome. Proposed correction: keep the entry framed as options under consideration unless a source documents a strike order or action.
proposed_correction: Trump Weighs Possible Further Strikes on Iran; Source Text Needed

title: Trump: At one Kentucky bar, young Republicans wrestle with their disappointment in Trump and their party
description_short: Trump: At one Kentucky bar, young Republicans wrestle with their disappointment in Trump and their party
description_medium: Young Republicans in Kentucky met at a local bar for their monthly political discussion as they weighed disappointment with Donald Trump and their party. The report presents the group’s gathering as a snapshot of internal Republican debate during Trump’s presidency. The available summary provides no names or examples of members’ views.
notes: Reason: The ABC page returned 404 and AP returned 403; the packet only says a Kentucky group meets monthly and is disappointed with Trump and the party. Proposed correction: add accessible article text with named or quoted views before writing the long account.
proposed_correction: Young Kentucky Republicans Discuss Disappointment with Trump and Their Party

title: Norway Moves Toward Formal FIFA Ethics Complaint Over Trump-Balogun Intervention
description_short: Norway Moves Toward Formal FIFA Ethics Complaint Over Trump-Balogun Intervention
description_medium: The Norwegian Football Association supported an ethics complaint against FIFA president Gianni Infantino after FIFA awarded Donald Trump its Peace Prize. The complaint alleged that the award violated FIFA’s political-neutrality rules. Norway’s action concerned the award and Infantino, separate from the FIFA decision about Folarin Balogun’s match ban.
subcategory: FIFA ethics complaint and political neutrality
notes: Reason: The supplied correction context identifies Norway’s letter supporting an ethics complaint against Infantino over FIFA’s Peace Prize for Trump; the AP page returned 403. The Balogun suspension was a separate story, not the subject of this complaint. Proposed correction: retitle around the Infantino complaint and do not connect it to the separate ban decision.
proposed_correction: Norway Supports FIFA Ethics Complaint Concerning Infantino and the FIFA Peace Prize

title: Trump Fires Bondi for Insufficient Weaponization — Epstein Files Buried Under New AG
description_short: Trump Fires Bondi for Insufficient Weaponization — Epstein Files Buried Under New AG
description_medium: On April 9, 2026, Melania Trump denied having a relationship with Jeffrey Epstein and urged Congress to hold a hearing for survivors. Her public statement called attention to survivors and congressional scrutiny of the case. NBC reported on the statement, which addressed neither Pam Bondi’s removal nor the Justice Department’s handling of Epstein records.
subcategory: Epstein-related DOJ actions and source mismatch
notes: Reason: The linked NBC article covers Melania Trump’s April 9 denial and request for a congressional hearing; it does not support the title’s April 2 Bondi removal, Blanche statement, or claim that DOJ stopped pursuing the files. The chronology does not establish a coordinated cover-up. Proposed correction: source those separate claims or retitle around Melania’s statement.
proposed_correction: Use a Separate, Sourced Entry for the Bondi/Blanche Claims

title: New Tariffs Target Canada and Brazil
description_short: Administration launched aggressive tariffs on Canada and Brazil commodities citing forced labor and digital policy concerns. Analysts warned of significant economic uncertainty.
description_medium: On July 20, 2026, the United States announced a 50% tariff on $20 billion of Canadian products. The summary also groups Brazil measures under forced-labor and digital-policy concerns, though it names no affected goods or rate. Reuters’ headline speaks only to the Canadian tariff, so its report alone cannot explain a combined Canada-Brazil package.
subcategory: Tariff actions involving Canada and Brazil
notes: Reason: Reuters’ supplied headline reports a 50% tariff on $20 billion of Canadian goods; its page returned 401. The synopsis mentions Brazil but gives no products, rate, date, or formal finding, and does not establish a joint package. Proposed correction: split the Canadian tariff from any Brazilian measures unless evidence documents one package.
proposed_correction: New 50% Tariff on Canadian Goods; Brazil Measures Need Separate Sourcing
